A_general.open_code_note: The public repository contains connection guides, client integrations, and skills; it does not contain the hosted server implementation. Its published main-server tool list matches the endpoint reference, but it is not code for the deployed service.
other_official_servers: https://mcp.jotform.com/mcp-app — Forms MCP App; official docs describe the main tools except get_submissions, plus display_form, list_submissions, create_submission, get_embed_code, and get_teams.
https://mcp.jotform.com/form-backend — Form Backend endpoint; listed on the official developer overview, but not included in the repository's three-product-server description.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Jotform's official MCP guide says the main MCP server is free; the user's Jotform plan limits still apply. No separate MCP charge was found.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Jotform offers a Starter free plan, paid Bronze, Silver, and Gold plans, and Enterprise with custom pricing. The pricing page contains current plan details.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Jotform plan limits apply to MCP use. The official MCP documentation reports Enterprise support for up to 600 requests per minute. An October 2026 third-party listing reports 60 requests per minute for Free and 600 for Enterprise; Jotform's public MCP guide does not specify the Free rate.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Browser sign-in and approval are required. The account's existing access bounds what the AI tool can see and do. The documentation says workspace installation may require an administrator; HTTP 429 indicates too many requests. OAuth metadata lists readOnly and full scopes.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Jotform controls the service and rate limits; the account holder approves or revokes client access; organization administrators may restrict connections.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The endpoint tool reference declares readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, and openWorldHint annotations. Five tools are read-only; create_form, assign_form, and edit_form are writes, with edit_form marked destructiveHint=true. 2. No server-enforced confirmation parameter or confirmation flow is documented. The edit_form description asks for high-level natural-language instructions; this is guidance, not documented enforcement. 3. OAuth scopes are readOnly and full. Jotform documents that the connected account's permissions bound access, organizations may restrict connections, workspace installs may require admin installation, and a client can be revoked in Connected Apps. Token lifetime and redirect approval details were not found. 4. The main server and product endpoints have different tool sets. No toolset filter, read-only endpoint, sandbox setting, or regional endpoint for this server was found. 5. No MCP-specific PII masking or field exclusions were documented. The general privacy policy describes information handling and retention; it does not specify MCP response redaction. 6. The docs say plan limits apply and 429 means too many requests. Enterprise documentation states up to 600 requests per minute; third-party DevelopersDigest reports Free at 60/minute. analyze_submissions accepts limit (default 10000) and chunkIndex (default 0); get_submissions supports pagination and date filters. No other MCP call cost or truncation behavior was established. 7. Schemas define required fields and types, but server-side rejection or correction of unknown/malformed arguments was not documented. 8. MCP-specific audit logging and telemetry defaults/opt-out were not found. 9. No feedback, rating, survey, or report-to-vendor tool appears among the seven official main-server tools; no upsell message was found in the official tool descriptions. 10. The official tool descriptions include behavioral guidance. Separate Claude skills and Gemini instructions are distributed in the public repository, outside this endpoint. 11. No behavior-dependent memory or changing tool availability based on prior calls was documented. 12. The vendor documents multiple product endpoints with different tool sets; the input endpoint is the main server. 13. No arbitrary API, SQL, script, or raw-request tool appears in the official list.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official endpoint-specific tool reference at https://api.jotform.com/mcp/documentation/servers/default lists 7 tools; the official repository's main-server list also names 7. No catalogue-only actions were added. DevelopersDigest independently reports 7. Manufact reports 11 names, including form_list, create_submission, list_submissions, and display_form; the official repository assigns several of these to the separate Forms App endpoint, so they are not counted for this input endpoint. Claude's publisher-verified connector directory lists 11 tools, also mixing names assigned by Jotform to another endpoint. Other catalogues reviewed either did not expose a complete tool list or required sign-in.

E_aggregated.token_method: Serialized the official endpoint tool-definition JSON (15,324 characters) and divided by four; no initialize instructions were available to include.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The documented main-server tools do not offer workflow/Jotflow editing; a Jotform support thread says workflow editing is not yet available through that surface. The published MCP tools also do not expose all Jotform plan, administration, export, or configuration functions. Jotform's product documentation and REST API describe broader product capabilities, but their parameters are not MCP tool parameters.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The tool reference steers agents toward specific tools, filters, defaults, and chunking behavior. Examples include “Do NOT use this tool for simply listing or browsing submissions—use list_submissions instead” and “When the response contains \"hasMore\": true you MUST immediately call this tool again”. These are tool-description instructions; no server enforcement of agent compliance is documented.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The access guide says: “Your AI tool sees what your Jotform account can see. It cannot do more than your account can.” It also documents Connected Apps revocation. The privacy policy describes general data retention and disclosure practices but does not specifically state MCP retention, training, or audit policies.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The official developer page describes remote MCP endpoints using Streamable HTTP and OAuth sign-in. The repository describes browser sign-in and says users do not paste passwords or API keys.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth-protected-resource metadata and the 401 response support authentication being required. Account-permission inheritance and revocation are documented behavior, but the hosted implementation is closed, so enforcement details beyond observed metadata and endpoint response cannot be checked. Tool-level behavioral rules are documented but are not shown to be enforced by the server.

contradictions: Manufact and Claude's publisher-verified connector directory list 11 tools for Jotform, while Jotform's official main-server reference lists 7. The official repository assigns tools such as create_submission, list_submissions, and display_form to the separate Forms App endpoint; these catalogue lists appear to combine endpoint variants.

The supplied OAuth metadata lists both readOnly and full scopes, while the main endpoint's official tool reference includes write actions. The scopes describe authorization options, not the currently granted scope for a particular connection.
observations_for_research: The main server and related product endpoints separate tool availability by product and workflow; the official docs also describe a same-tool-set /default alias for the Gemini extension.
The seven main-server tools include natural-language operations (create_form, edit_form, analyze_submissions) alongside retrieval and assignment tools.
The analyze_submissions description specifies an agent-directed continuation loop for chunked outputs, including an instruction not to respond until all chunks have been collected.
notes: Checked links.json, pages/ and code/ first, including the endpoint-specific tool reference, official MCP docs, official GitHub repository, pricing, privacy, support threads, and catalogues. The repository is a client/integration and documentation repository, not the hosted server implementation; its commit hash is recorded as the latest collected repository commit. The authorization-server metadata fetch was malformed in the supplied evidence, so DCR, PKCE, grants, token lifetime, and revocation metadata were not established. Unofficial community server and Klavis documentation were found but excluded as evidence. No initialize instructions were available. The actions file contains the 7 official tools for the input endpoint.
